x_failures: Cites Suchten p.97 for the Archeus 'fails to separate the pure from the impure' leading to tartar, gout and kidney stones; the page says only that De Tartaro discusses how the stomach is fortified to digest difficult things. Also says the Archeus separates essentia from stercus, citing Pharmacandi p.14, which names the stomach, not the Archeus.
y_failures: Cites van Helmont's Ortus p.665 for the Archeus as 'master Vulcan', but the page has no such phrase. Says Pharmacandi 'explicitly compares... the Archeus to the smith-god Vulcan', but the page calls the stomach the Vulcan. Has Paracelsus argue that 'the good sap, and the excrement, and the tartar are one and the same substance', which is van Helmont's own argument against Paracelsus on p.183.
reason: Both answers wrongly attribute claims to their cited pages. Y quotes Paracelsus's 'master Vulcan' passage accurately, links more relevant pages (Pharmacandi pp.13–14 and two van Helmont pages), and answers more fully, so it serves the reader slightly better despite misattributing van Helmont's view to Paracelsus.
